$note: Build sheet for Nod 0.8.0 (n8n-io/nod, Apache-2.0, tag nod-v0.8.0, commit f6f86be2, 2026-11-16), n8n labs' personal agent with its own Linux workspace and Chromium. Upstream self-host (deployment/self-host/compose.yaml) runs server + postgres + workspace + browser + a filtered Docker-socket proxy, and the server reaches workspace and browser ONLY via `docker exec -i` (src/providers/docker/command.ts:278, src/providers/container-browser/index.ts:37). Railway has no Docker socket and one volume per service, so: (1) the server image replaces the docker CLI with relay/docker, a shim that forwards exactly those two exec shapes over the private network; (2) workspace and browser each run relay/nod-relay-agent.mjs as root, which checks a shared token, applies upstream docker-proxy.mjs's allow rules, drops to uid node (or the 2xxxx:1002 connected-CLI uids) and returns stdio + exit code; (3) the workspace's two upstream volumes (/workspace, /home/node) share one Railway volume via a /home/node symlink. Every server-to-workspace file operation already goes through exec stdio (artifactRead/WriteProgram), so no shared volume is needed. Upstream publishes no images; .github/workflows/images.yml builds upstream's own Dockerfiles at the pinned tag and layers the relay on top. Lost vs upstream: workspace-network (iptables egress firewall, needs NET_ADMIN, which Railway does not grant), so workspace commands can reach the project's private network; every service there is token- or password-protected. Policy gate CLEAR (2026-11-16): the agent acts on the deployer's own accounts and sites they name, asks before acting, and sends nothing unprompted.
name: Nod

source.$note: Upstream deployment/self-host/Dockerfile + relay/docker shim + images/server-entry.sh (chowns the volume, derives NOD_VAULT_KEY, writes the relay config, drops to node).

deploy.$note: No healthcheckPath: Nod 403s any Host other than NOD_PUBLIC_URL's (src/server/access.ts:90), and Railway's prober sends Host: healthcheck.railway.app; /api/health also requires the bearer token. Restart on failure covers a server that boots before Postgres.

NOD_AUTH_TOKEN.description: Access token for the web app and desktop app. Paste it into the sign-in form. Must be 43+ letters, digits, - or _.

NOD_VAULT_SEED.$note: Nod needs NOD_VAULT_KEY as canonical base64 of exactly 32 bytes (src/providers/environment/key-store.ts), which secret() cannot emit; server-entry.sh derives it as base64(sha256(seed)). Setting NOD_VAULT_KEY directly overrides the seed.
NOD_VAULT_SEED.description: Seed for the Vault encryption key. Back it up: saved credentials cannot be decrypted without it.

NOD_RELAY_TOKEN.description: Shared secret between Nod and its Workspace and Browser services.

NOD_PUBLIC_URL.description: Exact public origin. Nod rejects requests for any other host.

NOD_WORKSPACE_RELAY.description: Private address of the Workspace relay.

NOD_BROWSER_RELAY.description: Private address of the Browser relay.

NOD_HOST.$note: Dual-stack: Railway's edge and private network dial IPv6.

WORKSPACE_CONTAINER.description: Name the docker shim maps to the Workspace relay.

BROWSER_CONTAINER.description: Name the docker shim maps to the Browser relay.

NOD_ANALYTICS_ENABLED.description: Product analytics to n8n. Off, as in upstream self-host.

source.$note: Upstream Dockerfile.workspace (Python, Node, LibreOffice, ffmpeg, OCR) + nod-relay-agent.
Upstream Dockerfile.browser (Chromium under Xvfb, agent-browser worker) + nod-relay-agent. Sign-ins the agent makes persist in /data.
Railway's own Postgres image. Nod needs no extensions (gen_random_uuid is core since PG13); upstream pins postgres:17.

PGDATA.description: Data directory inside the volume (Railway volumes ship a lost+found at the root).
